blocks.x: Decision-grade reporting with one truth per metric: certified datasets, metric contracts with owners, and an executive layer fast enough that nobody rebuilds the number in a spreadsheet before the board meeting.
The spreadsheet shadow is a product of slow truth

Executive analytics fails as a numbers argument: three dashboards, five versions of revenue, a meeting spent reconciling spreadsheets. The cure is metric contracts — one definition, one certified dataset, one owner — and a semantic layer that makes the contract executable rather than a wiki page.

The build is unglamorous: certify the datasets behind the top metrics, wire the semantic layer, instrument the dispute rate, and retire the shadow spreadsheets on evidence. The payoff is meetings that start from the same number.
Below: the failure modes that multiply versions of the truth, the reference architecture that certifies metrics, and the console that tracks trust in the BI estate.
Four failure modes that multiply versions of the truth
Each of these grows the spreadsheet shadow — the countermeasures make certified metrics faster and more trusted than the private rebuild.

widgets.title: The BI semantic stack — click nodes for the governance contract

nodes.label: Gold layer
nodes.detail: Dimensional marts from the lakehouse with documented grain — the semantic layer sits on foundations, not on whatever query was fastest.

nodes.label: Semantic layer
nodes.detail: One definition per metric: formula, filters, grain, owner — versioned, tested against golden cases, consumed by every surface.

nodes.label: Certification tiers
nodes.detail: Decision-grade surfaces (audited lineage, freshness SLA, review cadence) vs exploratory — executives read certified, analysts explore with lineage.

nodes.label: Executive surfaces
nodes.detail: Review-ready dashboards rendered from certified metrics — the prep is 90 minutes because the numbers already agree.

nodes.label: Self-serve library
nodes.detail: Curated metric libraries and data products with row-level security from the identity fabric — governed breadth, not gated scarcity.

nodes.label: Adoption telemetry
nodes.detail: Usage by certification tier, query cost by team, retirement rate — the estate's truth about what is actually used.

nodes.label: Retirement registry
nodes.detail: Dashboards retired with usage evidence and owner sign-off — sprawl is pruned on cadence, not on crisis.

widgets.note: Click nodes for the contract each layer carries. The semantic layer is where the metric arguments go to be settled — permanently, as data.
